explanation: Curling your index finger to call someone over — the common Western 'come here' gesture — can come across as condescending or overly commanding in Russia, similar to summoning a child or a pet. Russians themselves more typically beckon with the palm facing down and fingers waving inward, rather than curling one finger upward.
local_tip: To call someone over, use a palm-down hand with fingers waving inward rather than crooking a single finger.

also_check.note: Beckoning with the index finger is considered very rude and used only for animals.
This gesture can be seen as a serious insult or challenge.
Common in casual settings but can seem condescending in formal or professional contexts.
